newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Death toll rises to 28 in Indonesia plane crash.
newsitem.headline: Death toll rises to 28 in Indonesia plane crash.

text.p: The death toll in an aircraft crash near the Indonesian city of Bandung rose to 28 on Friday after the death of an injured passenger, the official Antara news agency reported.
The Fokker F-27 chartered to Sempati Air crashed around midday on Thursday shortly after taking off from Bandung, about 120 km (75 miles) southeast of the capital Jakarta, the flight's destination.
"As of Friday morning...28 people have been reported as dead and 22 injured, including three local residents," the report said.
Aviation industry experts said there was reason to be concerned with the Indonesian aviation sector after the third civil aviation accident in as many months.

Three crew died last week when a Merpati C-212 crashed near Ambon, and 15 passengers and crew died when a British-built ATP, also operated by Merpati, crashed on its approach to Belitung island in April.
"These accidents, coming so close to one another, show a disturbing trend in either maintenance or pilot training," an expert familiar with the Indonesian aviation sector said.
"There is reason to be concerned," said the expert, who asked not to be identified.
Officials said they were still investigating the cause of Thursday's crash.
"According to eyewitnesses, it appears one engine had stopped," Sergeant Budiarjo from Bandung's Search and Rescue office told Reuters.
Transport Minister Haryanto Dhanutirto was quoted on Friday by Antara as saying after visiting the crash site that the pilot had signalled he wanted to "return to base" because an engine had stopped.
He said it appeared he had then attempted to make an emergency landing at an air force base about one km (less than a mile) from the crash site.
All five crew, including pilot and co-pilot, died.
Malaysian businessman Jacky Pak told Reuters from his hospital bed that he had seen the left engine catch fire on the Fokker minutes before the crash.
"I remember passengers crying, praying and screaming before the aircraft crashed. After that I just remember waking up in the ambulance on the way to hospital," Pak said.
Many of the survivors in hospital suffered burns as the aircraft, owned by local charter operator PT Trigana Air Service, exploded soon after impact.
